title: Ingress DNS-proxy Terraform proposal and upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a lightweight DNS-proxy placed alongside the ingress fleet for private (VPC + on-prem) deployments, documents the Terraform module shape we want, and provides an upgrade and rollback checklist for moving from the current split-horizon DNS + NAT approach to a dns-proxy-based flow. Goal: reduce DNS leakage, centralize split-horizon resolution per-customer, and enable per-tenant DNS policy (block lists, upstream selection) without touching cluster-level resolv.conf hacks.

Context and motivation:
- Current pain: Several customers running private deployments have fragile on-host DNS changes (resolv.conf rewrites, dnsmasq churn) that break when we upgrade node images or install sidecars.
- Need: a controlled, auditable, Terraform-managed deploy of a dns-proxy that terminates DNS queries locally (127.0.0.1) and forwards selectively to internal resolvers or customer on-prem resolvers over mTLS or a secure tunnel.
- Secondary benefits: faster failover for internal names, consistent caching to reduce egress to cloud DNS, and simplified audit for egress DNS access.

Target topology (high-level):
- Ingress nodes run: ingress-controller (nginx/contour/our runtime) + dns-proxy daemonset (single-threaded, low mem).
- DNS path: app -> container /etc/resolv.conf -> loopback 127.0.0.1:5300 -> dns-proxy -> policy -> selected upstream (VPC resolver or onprem-over-tunnel).
- Egress NAT: egress from dns-proxy to upstreams should be from predictable IP (egress IP via SNAT in NAT gateway or egress pod IP with egress policy).

Design decisions (short):
- Use a daemonset (hostNetwork: true) so node-local apps can reach 127.0.0.1:5300.
- Avoid cluster-wide resolv.conf changes. The ingress container images will be configured to use 127.0.0.1 explicitly where possible; otherwise we provide a small sidecar that sets DNS for the process via /etc/hosts or LD_PRELOAD (last resort).
- Upstreams: Support multiple upstreams with priorities and options for mTLS tunnel (wireguard/mtls-proxy) for on-prem resolvers.
- Caching TTL: configurable with defaults tuned to reduce burst load (cache min-ttl: 5s, default-ttl: 60s, max-ttl: 5m).
- Split-horizon: rules keyed by domain suffix and by tenant label on the request path (SNI + source IP mapping).

Terraform module sketch (interface):
- Module name: redwood_private_ingress_dns_proxy
- Entry variables (high level):
  - name_prefix (string)
  - namespace (string)
  - replicas (number)
  - image (string)
  - cpu_request (string)
  - mem_request (string)
  - host_network (bool)
  - upstreams (list(object))  # object with {name, endpoint, port, tls_enabled, expected_cn}
  - split_horizon_rules (list(object)) # {domain, upstream_name, tenant_id}
  - egress_nat_ip (string) # optional: reserved NAT IP for dns-proxy egress
  - network_policies_enabled (bool)
  - service_account (string)
  - tolerations, node_selector (map)

- Outputs:
  - daemonset_name
  - service_name (ClusterIP for local test)
  - pod_security_policy (if any)

Example (pseudo-Terraform usage):
module "ingress_dns_proxy" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//ingress-dns-proxy"
  name_prefix = "redwood-ingress"
  namespace = "ingress-system"
  replicas = 3
  image = "gcr.io/redwood/dns-proxy:2026-02-18"
  host_network = true
  upstreams = [
    { name = "vpc-resolver", endpoint = "169.254.169.253", port = 53, tls_enabled = false },
    { name = "customer-1-onprem", endpoint = "10.200.0.2", port = 853, tls_enabled = true, expected_cn = "resolver.customer1.example" },
  ]
  split_horizon_rules = [
    { domain = "internal.redwood.local", upstream_name = "vpc-resolver", tenant_id = "" },
    { domain = "*.customer1.svc", upstream_name = "customer-1-onprem", tenant_id = "customer1" },
  ]
}

Implementation notes for the Terraform module (non-exhaustive):
- Create the k8s/daemonset resource using k8s_manifest provider or helm release (pin chart version). Pin everything.
- Create a ConfigMap with the full policy file (domain -> upstream mapping) and mount readOnly.
- If hostNetwork=true, be extra explicit about port collisions (5300) and require nodeSelector/tolerations for ingress nodes only.
- Provide a toggle to emit a ClusterIP service for testing (not used in hostNetwork mode).
- Provide a resource to reserve an egress IP (cloud-specific) and attach SNAT rule so dns-proxy upstream traffic uses that IP. Document cloud provider differences in the README.

Network/security rules needed (summary):
- Firewall/SGs (cloud): allow egress from dns-proxy egress IP to configured upstream ports (53/853), restrict to upstream IPs only.
- Ingress node firewall: allow 127.0.0.1:5300 local, disallow node-level UDP:53 from arbitrary pods (enforce via network policy).
- NetworkPolicy (K8s):
  - Allow dns-proxy pods to talk to upstream egress endpoints (via egress rule to IPBlocks).
  - Deny all other pods in ingress namespace from talking outbound on port 53/853 (to force use of dns-proxy).
  - If using Cilium, prefer L7 policy to block non-dns flows and trace resolution.
- Host-level: ensure conntrack table and ephemeral port limits are acceptable for caching upstream queries.

Upgrade and cutover checklist (step-by-step):
1) Pre-flight (planning, ~1 week window):
   - Confirm ticket: JIRA-INFRA-1123 created and owner assigned.
   - Validate terraform modules pass static checks (tflint) and module tests.
   - Build dns-proxy image and push to registry (tagged). Create image-SBOM and vuln scan report.
   - Prepare a canary node pool (2-3 nodes) labeled ingress-canary.
   - Create a test plan and roll-back plan in the ticket.

2) Smoke deploy to staging (day -3):
   - Apply module to staging cluster using a feature branch of terraform.
   - Verify dns-proxy daemonset scheduling on canary nodes only.
   - Verify basic resolution: kubectl exec into ingress pod and nslookup internal names -> respond.
   - Verify caching behavior: repeated lookup reduces egress, verify Prometheus metric dns_proxy_cache_hits_count.

3) Canary in prod (day 0):
   - Apply module with node_selector for ingress-canary in prod. replicas = 1 per canary node.
   - Update a small subset of ingress instances (canary traffic) to use 127.0.0.1:5300 explicitly (configmap tweak).
   - Monitor: DNS latencies, cache hit rate, egress bytes, error rate for ingress routes.
   - Run integration tests: certificate issuance (if name uses ACME via internal resolver), and TLS handshakes that probe SNI->upstream path.

4) Gradual rollout (48-72h):
   - Shift more ingress nodes into node pool with dns-proxy. Use terraform plan/apply to scale replicas and nodeSelector.
   - Every batch (10–20% nodes): run live traffic smoke tests and A/B checks.
   - Watch for: increased NXDOMAIN for internal names, TTL misconfigurations, egress firewall denies.

5) Final cutover (weekend/low traffic):
   - Remove old node-level resolv.conf updates (if any) and apply NetworkPolicy to block outbound 53/853 from ingress namespace except dns-proxy.
   - Ensure egress NAT IPs are in place and firewall rules updated.
   - Run end-to-end tests for each major customer with custom DNS paths.

6) Post-cutover checks (24–72h):
   - Ensure cache hit rate > target (50–80% depending on workload).
   - No unhandled NXDOMAIN regressions reported by customer teams.
   - Roll forward any additional split-horizon rules discovered in logs.

Rollback plan (fast):
- If DNS queries fail at >1% across ingress, revert terraform (use saved plan) and scale dns-proxy daemonset to 0, re-apply node-level resolv.conf change (stored in repo).
- Also have a fail-open emergency: temporarily change ingress containers to use cluster-dns IP directly (coord with SRE).

Testing and observability checklist:
- Metrics: dns_query_count, dns_query_latency_seconds_bucket, dns_proxy_cache_hits_count, upstream_failure_count, tls_handshake_failures_count.
- Logs: annotate logs with tenant_id and request_id. Capture 1% of full queries for privacy review.
- Tracing: instrument upstream forwarding with trace id and attach to request logs; correlate with ingress request ids.
- Alerts: upstream_failure_count > 5/min for 5m, cache_miss_rate > 90% for 15m, dns_latency_p50 > 200ms for 10m.

Edge cases and operational notes:
- On-prem resolvers behind load balancers with client-subnet sensitivity: preserve EDNS-CLIENT-SUBNET if required and document privacy trade-offs.
- If an onprem resolver rejects TLS with SNI mismatch, fall back to tunneled UDP via wireguard endpoint and route through NAT; require operator manual approval.
- IPv6: ensure module supports dual-stack and that egress NAT rules are implemented per-cloud semantics.
- Container runtime: when using hostNetwork=true, DNS listen port collisions with host services must be guarded by node labels and a terraform plan guardrail.

Sample NetworkPolicy (k8s pseudo-yaml for operators) – for docs only (we will convert into Terraform k8s_network_policy resource):
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: block-ingress-dns-direct
  namespace: ingress-system
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [ "Egress" ]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: { app: dns-proxy }
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 853

Operational runbook snippets (quick commands):
- Terraform plan/apply (module in feature branch):
  git checkout feature/dns-proxy-module
  terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=tfplan
  terraform apply tfplan

- Verify pods: kubectl -n ingress-system get ds -l app=dns-proxy
- Test resolution from ingress pod: kubectl exec -n ingress-system -it ingress-pod -- nslookup internal.someapp.redwood.local 127.0.0.1#5300

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a per-tenant policy UI in Console to manage split-horizon rules, or should that live in config-as-code only? (UX/PM decision).
- Decide: mTLS vs wireguard for on-prem upstream security. mTLS easier to audit, wireguard simpler for large UDP flows.
- How to handle PTR / reverse lookups for auditing purposes in split-horizon scenarios?

References and related tickets:
- JIRA-INFRA-1123: dns-proxy design and rollout plan (owner: Aisha Patel)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/87 (ingress-dns-proxy initial module)
- Confluence: Ingress DNS Proxy Design (diagram + failure modes)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: we prefer node-local daemonset using hostNetwork and explicit node labeling over cluster-wide mutation of resolv.conf.
- Focus review on: upstream security model, firewall/egress NAT patterns per cloud, and any compliance issues for caching resolution results.

Action items (next steps):
- [Aisha] finalize module variables list and submit PR for module skeleton (target: 2026-02-26).
- [Jun] prototype egress NAT IP reservation scripts for AWS/GCP (target: 2026-03-05).
- [Marta] run vulnerability scan on dns-proxy image and report findings (target: 2026-02-28).
- [SRE] schedule canary window and notify on-call rotation (target before prod canary).

End of draft.
